bottleneck_assessment.inference: Prefill is the highest-value first target for this trace. Testing microbatch 128 and 256 at fixed threads isolates fewer/larger prompt decode batches; prompt_threads=8 then probes prompt parallelism. A decode_threads=2 screen isolates generation-thread count but cannot remove a prefill bottleneck.
bottleneck_assessment.limits: One request does not establish a general distribution. The frozen synthetic 24-state screen is for bounded runtime comparison, not model quality or human acceptance.
bottleneck_assessment.observed: One real 321-token failed request spent about 1.715 s in prompt evaluation and 0.333 s generating 13 tokens; current changed-state aggregate median is 0.874 s, with a 2.689 s p95.

existing_thinkpad_performance_evidence.comparison_caveat: Earlier trained-layout screening had 2404 ms median / 3683 ms p95 for changed states; this is historical context, not a same-run causal estimate or quality claim.

repack_investigation.avx2_candidate: The pinned llama.cpp CPU repack selector has a Q4_K path for AVX2 (Q4_K 8x8) when tensor width is divisible by 8; ThinkPad flags include AVX2.
repack_investigation.reason: Pinned llama-cpp-sys build script documents OFF as preserving the original mmap-friendly weight layout rather than runtime repacking into anonymous RAM, useful when mmap-streaming a model larger than RAM.
repack_investigation.screen_status: Not in the six-setting frozen run. Per-setting binary hashes are recorded so a separately frozen candidate can be evaluated without conflating binary identities.
repack_investigation.tradeoff: Potential prefill/matmul speedup is unmeasured; repacking can increase anonymous process/cgroup memory and reduce mmap advantages. Compare only with a separate attested executable and capture RSS/PSS plus cgroup memory and swap.
